scenes.intro: Hello, Samantha. Your financial health score is 82 out of 100, and Sherpas calls that strong. Over the next few minutes you'll see your plan drawn as your own home, from the foundations to the roof. We'll walk through each part and what it means for you, Ethan and Ava.
scenes.pillar_savings_and_cash_flow: Your plumbing is solid. Savings and cash flow scores 22 out of 30 points. You save 24% of your income, a strong habit, but your outgoings run about $6,418 a year short, and none of that saving goes into retirement accounts yet. In practice, your everyday cash has to cover that gap each year.
scenes.pillar_debt: Your walls are solid. Debt scores 20 out of 20 points. You carry no debt, and your home is owned outright with $900,000 of equity. No loan payments pull at your monthly cash. Even so, only $750 of your cash sits above both your reserve and your goals coming up soon, so there is little slack.
scenes.pillar_investments: Your garden is cracked, and investments score 10 out of 15 points. Most of your wealth is your home, about 65% of it, and a home is not easy to spend. Your invested savings sit at 85.1% in stocks, a little above the 80.0% you aim for. College and retirement both have to come out of the same everyday cash.
scenes.pillar_liquidity_and_emergency_fund: Your foundations are solid, and your emergency fund scores 15 out of 15 points. Your cash covers 7.9 months of essential expenses, more than the 5 to 6 months suggested. Once you set aside the goals coming up soon, that cover falls to 6.1 months, so a surprise bill would eat into it faster than you might think.
scenes.pillar_insurance_and_protection: Your roof is solid, and insurance and protection scores 14 out of 20 points. You hold $2,000,000 of term life cover, within the range recommended for your household, protecting Ethan and Ava if your income ever stopped. Underneath your umbrella, the cover behind your home and auto policies shows as unconfirmed, so a large claim could reach your own money.
scenes.move_1: A step your plan already worked out: adding homeowners insurance on your main home, which closes a gap in your cover. It repairs your roof and lifts your score from 82 out of 100 to 84 out of 100.
scenes.move_2: Another step in the plan: spreading out the money you hold in a single fund, trimming it from 39% to 25% of your investments. That repairs your garden and moves your score from 82 out of 100 to 83 out of 100.
scenes.move_3: The plan also shifts your mix from 85% in stocks to 80%, moving about $17,100. That repairs your garden, lifting your score from 82 out of 100 to 83 out of 100.
scenes.timeline: Now look ahead, Samantha. You plan to retire at 65, and on this plan your savings and investments run out at age 73, with $1,448,673 of planned spending unpaid by the end. The plan shows no debt from 2059. Those later years are where the pressure sits, since college for Ethan and Ava competes for the same dollars.
